fatal_errors: The proposed 1–2 at% Hf/Zr intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated Re addition to sputtered NbMoTaW films.
The cited evidence does not establish that trace Hf or Zr creates coherent precipitates, improves ductility, preserves 1600 °C performance, or enhances irradiation resistance in NbMoTaW.
The hypothesis simultaneously requires retention of a single-phase BCC structure and formation of precipitates or phase heterogeneities, without resolving this structural inconsistency.
The irradiation prediction lacks a defined particle, energy, fluence, temperature, and damage profile, so it is not comparable to the target 120 keV He irradiation regime.
Bulk arc-melted and thermomechanically processed alloys are not an appropriate reconstruction of the nanocrystalline magnetron-sputtered film system.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation objectives and includes a nominal baseline and falsification rule, but it is an essentially speculative alternative rather than a reconstruction. The target intervention was equiatomic Re addition in nanocrystalline sputtered films, where grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions suppressed grain-boundary He-bubble accumulation and irradiation embrittlement. The proposed Hf/Zr precipitate mechanism has little agreement with that mechanism and is not supported by the cited literature: E1 concerns Hf-containing precipitates in FCC alloys, E2 discusses other refractory alloy systems, and E3 only shows that Hf/Zr-containing RHEAs can be ductile. None validates preservation of NbMoTaW performance at 1600 °C or under irradiation. The experiment could test the broad proposition, but its irradiation protocol is insufficiently specified and allowing a simulation in place of irradiation weakens discrimination.
